habitat: 만, 강 하구, 툰드라 해안의 호수
summary: 툰드라 지역 해안의 호수와 만, 강 하구에 살고 겨울에는 주로 만에서 지내는 새로, 기러기만 한 크기로 아비류 가운데 가장 크다. 작은 섬이나 물가 땅의 물풀 사이에 풀과 이끼로 잘 숨긴 둥지를 짓고 올리브빛이 도는 갈색 알을 2개 낳는다. 전북구의 북쪽 연안 툰드라와 북아메리카, 알래스카, 오호츠크 해안 등지에서 번식한다.

art.subject: Yellow-billed Loon (Gavia adamsii), adult in winter (non-breeding) plumage, as seen off Korean coasts from November to March: crown and hindneck pale greyish-brown; face pale around the eye with a darker smudge on the ear coverts; throat, foreneck and underparts white, merging diffusely into the brown hindneck; upperparts plain dark grey-brown with faint paler feather edges; bill large, pale ivory-yellow, the straight upper edge staying pale to the tip and the lower mandible angled upward, so the bill looks upturned; dark eye; legs hidden under water.
art.scene: sheltered bay on the Korean east coast in winter, calm grey-blue water under low winter light; no people, buildings or text
views: adult winter, side view swimming low: pale greyish-brown head and hindneck, white throat and foreneck, dark grey-brown back, large pale ivory-yellow bill that looks upturned

adult breeding (summer, rarely seen in Korea), side view swimming: black head and neck glossed purple-green, broken white stripes on the neck, rows of white spots on the back, scapulars and flanks, bright yellow bill
adult, head close-up in profile: straight pale upper mandible and angled lower mandible giving an upturned look, pale to the tip
adult winter in flight, seen from below: white belly and underparts, pale bill, large feet projecting beyond the tail; head, neck, body and feet in a straight line
art.build: Very large, heavy diver, about 84–97cm, goose-sized and the largest loon, bulkier than Black-throated Loon (Gavia arctica). Swims low in the water with a thick neck and a big, angular head with a steep forehead and a bump on the crown. Bill long, heavy and dagger-shaped, about as long as the head, held tilted slightly upward. Legs set far back, used only for swimming. In flight hunch-backed, with large feet projecting beyond the tail.
avoid: Do not paint a dark culmen or a blackish bill — that is Common Loon (Gavia immer); the Yellow-billed Loon's bill is pale to the tip.
Do not paint a small, slender bill or a small head (Black-throated or Pacific Loon).
Do not show breeding plumage on a winter sea scene; in winter the head and neck are pale brown and white.
Do not show the bird standing on land or with legs under the body.
